Small Business Subchapter V Elections Up 46% in 2026 as Middle District of Florida (Orlando) Leads the Country in Filings More Central Florida business owners are finding out about Subchapter V before it’s too late for them to use it. ORLANDO, FL, UNITED STATES, November 5, 2026 /EINPresswire.com/ — National small business Subchapter V of Chapter 11 elections are up 46% through the first 9 months of 2026 vs. 2025, with 2,442 filings, according to data provider Epiq, as reported. And the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Middle District of Florida (Orlando Federal Bankruptcy Court) is in the lead for Subchapter V filings. According to the court’s own newsletter, the number of Subchapter V cases here is 324 for the 12 months through June 30, 2026. That’s for Central Florida, says Orlando-based bankruptcy law firm Juan Burgos Law. Subchapter V is a simplified Chapter 11 filing for small businesses. It allows the business owner to maintain control of the business while proposing a repayment plan (no competing creditor-created plan, in most cases). There’s a court-appointed trustee to help. The maximum amount of debt that can qualify for Subchapter V is currently $3,424,000. The new Bankruptcy Threshold Adjustment Act (H.R. 7730), passed by Congress, would increase that to $7.5M. But it hasn’t gone into effect yet. (As of November 5, 2026, still waiting for the President to sign.) “More Central Florida business owners are finding out about Subchapter V before it’s too late for them to use it,” says Juan Burgos Law founder Juan C. Burgos. “The current debt limit is too low for a business that might have $4 or $5M of debt today. But maybe the law’s about to change that. Either way, timing and debt type are important. That’s the kind of question you can get an answer for in a short case review.” Juan Burgos Law represents clients in English, Spanish, and Portuguese. The firm has a plain-language guide for Central Florida business owners about Subchapter V. It includes a version in Spanish for the Hispanic business community here in the area. Juan Burgos Law handles Chapter 7, 11, 13 and Subchapter V cases in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Middle District of Florida. title: Before GTA VI comes out, I'm playing the entirety of GTA V completely in my web browser - XDA
content: With Grand Theft Auto VI just days away, it's astonishing that GTA V is still coming up with brand-new ways to play. Over the past few months, it's striking how the boundaries of PC gaming have become increasingly arbitrary. Browser-based games are all the rage today, especially with the barrage of AAA ports that are flooding Chrome and Firefox. And yet, nothing could have prepared me for having Grand Theft Auto V running in a browser tab. Somehow, all it took to start playing one of the greatest AAA games ever made was opening a new tab in Chrome and waiting a few minutes. I've tested my fair share of browser-based game projects, so I went into this one expecting the usual compromises. Truth be told, I fully expected to be able to play just a small section of Los Santos, with maybe a handful of playable mechanics. Instead, GTA V loaded up with surprisingly little fuss, and I found myself staring at an experience that felt considerably closer to the real thing. In fact, the initial process was shockingly frictionless. Within a couple of minutes, I was playing the actual campaign. This wasn't a decoy or rip-off, either — Michael, Trevor, and the gang were fully storming the bank and escaping the police as I played through the entire GTA V prologue. I even expected the game to cut out or loop on itself after the prologue, but minutes later, I was playing as Franklin, repossessing cars and driving around a tow truck. There's even a sandbox mode, and it dropped me straight into a random section of Los Santos, giving me a full stack of weapons, cheats, and the freedom to explore the entire map. That was particularly useful, too, since nothing clears your head like loading up the sandbox mode and blowing up anything that moves with a grenade launcher and God Mode turned on. Ultimately, though, having this option available through a browser tab is still difficult to wrap my head around. After getting over the sheer novelty of running GTA V in a browser, one of the first things I noticed was how familiar everything felt. The keyboard controls were exactly what I'd expect from the Windows PC version, with no awkward remapping or bizarre input behavior getting between Los Santos and me. My muscle memory, built over thirteen years, kicked in almost immediately. Getting my controller working was equally painless. I plugged in my DualSense, and had Windows recognize it as an Xbox controller (DS4Windows starts at boot). From there, everything worked as expected, including the familiar button mappings. Of course, getting GTA V running in a browser doesn't mean every part of the experience is perfect. Throughout my time playing, I kept running into graphical oddities. It was easy to ignore the occasional missing road texture since I could just drive away, but it was much more immersion-breaking when I entered a full area with zero building textures and roads floating an inch above my car. Clearly, GTA V on a web browser is pretty buggy — cars in traffic were popping in and out of thin air, and some were driving while halfway embedded in the road. At times, it almost felt like playing Cyberpunk 2077 at release in 2020. Of course, this was much more forgivable, since this was still a proper AAA game that I could close by pressing Ctrl+W in my browser. Thankfully, most of these issues weren't persistent. Respawning my character usually brought missing assets back into place, although having to deliberately die to fix graphical glitches isn't exactly my idea of troubleshooting. What was even more surprising was that the game also offered graphics settings, instead of locking me into whatever configuration the browser port considered appropriate. I could monitor GPU utilization and VRAM consumption while playing, too, which made for an interesting hardware experiment. Curiously, GTA V in the web browser actually took up around 6 GB of VRAM from my RTX 4070 Ti, all while my GPU utilization never crossed 20%. The whole time, though, it ran at a smooth 60 FPS, no matter how much I cranked up the in-game settings. Over the past decade, GTA V's online multiplayer has arguably been the main reason for its continued success and why it remains as relevant as ever today. That's the one significant omission from this browser-based GTA V experience. You can't jump into GTA Online like you can if you played the original Halo: Combat Evolved in a browser. This is strictly a single-player affair. And yet, I still don't think that takes away from what makes this project so impressive. GTA V's single-player sandbox has always been entertaining enough to warrant revisiting, even when you've exhausted its campaign and have absolutely no interest in completing another mission. What really gets me is how accessible the whole thing is. You don't need to download dozens of gigabytes, configure an emulator, or spend an afternoon troubleshooting compatibility issues. There's also the rather awkward question of legality. These browser-based ports operate in a legal grey area, particularly when they rely on reverse-engineered code and original game assets. This one, though, is clearly illegal, and there are no two ways about it. Rockstar certainly hasn't authorized anyone to distribute GTA V through a browser link, so you should expect this project to become inaccessible any time now. That said, the open-source nature of some of these projects means clones and mirrors could surface almost as quickly (if not faster) as the original disappears. Enjoy the novelty while it lasts, because I wouldn't count on this particular link staying alive forever. The "huge GTA fan" reportedly won't make it to the anticipated game's release. It's almost poetic how just days before Grand Theft Auto VI finally comes out, the previous entry, which remains Rockstar's biggest cash cow today, is perfectly playable for free inside a browser. In fact, some would say that Rockstar and Sony started this landslide of PC ports and decompilations in the first place, with the former deciding to forgo a physical disc release for GTA VI and the latter going all-digital for all post-2028 games. I, for one, can't wait to boot up Jason and Lucia's adventure in GTA VI, come November 19. In the meantime, though, a single new tab in Chrome or Firefox will help me pay my respects and bid goodbye to Los Santos, the city that's been a playground for millions of players for the past thirteen years. title: How Porsche Helped Harley-Davidson Build The V-Rod's Engine - AOL.com
content: The names Harley-Davidson and Porsche carry as much weight in automotive circles as any manufacturers in the history of moving vehicles. The iconic brands, of course, hold sway over decidedly different segments of the automotive markets, with Harley-Davidson making its name in the motorcycle game, and Porsche earning renown for producing automobiles. Given the disparate focus of their manufacturing outputs, Harley-Davidson and Porsche hardly seemed like obvious partners for collaboration. Yet, in the early 2000s, the automotive titans indeed got together to combine their talents in the name of creating Harley's famed V-Rod cruiser. Turns out, the V-Rod was not actually the first time the companies had gone hive-mind for a Harley build, with the motorcycle maker turning to Porsche in the 1970s to help develop the innovative, but ultimately abandoned Nova engine. Developed in part to woo younger riders enthralled by powerful Japanese and American bikes and attract younger riders, the V-Rod (or VRSC as it was officially named) ran on one of the more unique and powerful engine's in the company's history — one that found Porsche and Harley-Davidson engineers collaborating to transform the latter's VR1000 Superbike racing engine into a street ready, liquid-cooled 120 horsepower monster capable of devouring any blacktop if encountered. Porsche's engineers also equipped the DOHC four-valve V-twin engine with dual overhead cams and fuel injection, making it a true rarity in Harley's legendary lineup of bikes. Read more: Here's What Happened To The Cast Of American Chopper After The Show Ended The aptly named Revolution engine was the first water-cooled motor to power a Harley-Davidson, arriving in stark contrast to the air-cooled Evolution engine that essentially saved Harley-Davidson from bankruptcy two decades prior. While the V-Rod was as loud and powerful as anything in the Harley-Davidson lineup, some diehard fans weren't ready to embrace the water-cooled Revolution, with the bike proving one of the manufacturer's more divisive builds when it hit showroom floors in 2002. Though the V-Rod's power was hard to ignore, some Harley-Davidson purists reportedly wanted little to do with the forward-thinking motorcycle, as some took issue with V-Rod's decidedly modern look (accented by a Fatboy back tire) and its radically re-designed engine. Even as some of Harley-Davidson's long-time fans were choosing to stay away from the souped-up cruiser, the V-Rod was hardly a failure in the manufacturer's lineup. In fact, the Revolution powered bike was apparently quite appealing to the market segment Harley-Davidson designed it for, with the company claiming the V-Rod was indeed attracting a younger, and more diverse consumer base to the brand. The numbers for Harley's powered by the Porsche-engineered Revolution engine must have been solid enough, as the bike maker continued to produce the divisive build for the better part of a 20-year span. In the end, Harley-Davidson bosses finally pulled the plug on both the V-Rod and the Revolution in 2017. Even as the bike and the engine failed to forever revolutionize the Harley-Davidson lineup, each continues to hold a unique place in the company's storied history. title: 20 years later, V For Vendetta is as prescient as ever - Bam Smack Pow
content: This refrain that started as a tribute to British anarchist Guy Fawkes became the catchphrase of the titular masked freedom fighter in Alan Moore’s iconic comic V For Vendetta. Originally published in 1982 in the British anthology comic Warrior before being republished by DC Comics. Moore created a vision of a dystopian future London and a hero named V, cloaked in a cape and Guy Fawkes mask, who teams with a teenage girl to free their country from the fascist leadership that oppresses them. Moore’s book was a direct reaction to the conservative leadership of Margaret Thatcher’s England. It would take more than two decades to bring the story to the big screen; however, it became clear elements needed to be tweaked to properly resonate with a modern audience. Enter the Wachowskis, fresh off the huge success of The Matrix trilogy and devoted comic book fans. They adapted Moore’s story with a more modern lens but a desire to remain true to the core themes of the original work. Keeping the setting of London but expanding the political commentary to be more broadly focused opened the story up to a wider audience. The film also uses many elements of George Orwell’s seminal dystopian novel 1984 in both design and story structure. This includes the clever casting of John Hurt (star of that novel’s film adaptation) as the High Chancellor of the villainous Norsefire political party who looms over the movie on massive screens. Something the movie retains from Moore’s comic is the mysterious and cipher-like hero of the story. Known only as V, we never see him out of his mask, his identity consciously a mystery to both the characters and the audience. Moore said he hid V’s name and face to keep him an enigma, as he wanted readers to come to their own conclusions about the nature of the central vendetta. We are only given the bare bones of V’s origin in shadowy flashbacks that more indicate the cruelty inflicted by the government than the specific details of who the man behind the mask was. He is one of many of tragic stories in this nightmare society. It is that symbology that contributes to the comic and film’s undying impact. The Guy Fawkes mask was given to the character by comics artist David Lloyd, who wanted him to be more of a freedom fighter than a traditional superhero. The iconography is key to the story, as the climax finds thousands of Londoners donning the mask to take to the streets in an act of rebellion against the totalitarian regime. V transcends being an individual and becomes a symbol of a movement, a desperate cry for freedom. Natalie Portman sums it up in her final lines in the film. When asked about V’s identity, she responds, “He was Edmond Dantes, and he was my father and my mother, my brother, and my friend. He was you and me. He was all of us.” This symbology has leapt off the page and screen in the two decades since the film’s release. The Guy Fawkes mask can be seen all over the world as a symbol of protest and a call for freedom. A legacy few fictional characters has been found in reality, which speaks to the potency of Moore’s original ideas and the brilliant adaptation that the Wachowskis and director James McTeague gave us. Though Moore, who is famously a bit prickly, made his complaints about the film known, I would argue the major changes made in the adaptation are what opened the story up to the world. The comic is certainly still a striking work of art, but reading it as an American in today’s era can feel somewhat distancing. The film, on the other hand, is as fresh as ever; it does simplify the central battle of oppression versus freedom but in a way that welcomes audiences rather than pandering to them. This is a deeply political film but not a specific one. The themes can be grasped in any culture and by all audiences that can connect to the battle for personal autonomy and individualism. If you have not seen the film, the good news is Warner Brothers Pictures is rereleasing it in theaters appropriately on November 5. Trust me when I say it still packs a punch, mixing political and moral ideas with adrenaline-pumping action that makes it one of the most engaging sci-fi movies to come out of a major studio. Phenomenal performances from an all-star cast, including Hugo Weaving, Natalie Portman, Stephen Fry, and many more, fill out the roster of incredible characters. It’s a movie that still has much to say and hopefully makes you ask a lot of questions. © 2026 Minute Media - All Rights Reserved. title: Constructive Receipt of Life Insurance Cash Surrender Value and Procedural Penalty Defenses: A Technical Analysis of Braun v. Commissioner - Current Federal Tax Developments
content: A site devoted to articles on current developments in federal taxes geared toward CPAs in tax practice. Robert E. Braun v. Commissioner of Internal Revenue, Docket No. 25467-21S (U.S. Tax Court Oct. 20, 2026) (Bench Opinion by STJ Diana L. Leyden) Tax practitioners frequently encounter clients who misapprehend the federal income tax consequences associated with whole life insurance policy conversions, lapse events, and policy loan offsets. In Braun v. Commissioner, Docket No. 25467-21S, the United States Tax Court evaluated whether a taxpayer realized ordinary income under Internal Revenue Code (I.R.C.) Section 72(e) when an insurer converted lapsed whole life policies into term insurance policies, using accumulated cash value to extinguish outstanding policy loans and purchase term coverage. Special Trial Judge Diana L. Leyden, rendering an oral bench opinion pursuant to I.R.C. Section 7459(b) and Tax Court Rule 152, held that the taxpayer constructively received taxable gross income to the extent the cash surrender value used in the transaction exceeded his basis (aggregate premiums paid). However, the Court ruled in favor of the taxpayer regarding the accuracy-related penalty under I.R.C. Section 6662(a) because the Commissioner failed to satisfy his statutory burden of production under I.R.C. Section 6751(b) regarding supervisory approval or automated penalty calculation. This decision offers important technical guidance for CPAs and Enrolled Agents regarding gross income realization under I.R.C. Section 61(a)(9), information return dispute mechanics under I.R.C. Section 6201(d), and mandatory penalty verification standards. Beginning in 1977, the taxpayer, Robert E. Braun, purchased whole life insurance policies from Northwestern Mutual Life Insurance Company. At the time of purchase, Mr. Braun operated under the understanding that paying policy premiums until reaching age 65 would entitle him to receive recurring annuity payments. In 1992, Mr. Braun left his employment at a banking institution to write books on banking full-time. Subsequent changes in publisher compensation structures caused a substantial drop in his earnings. To maintain his living expenses and continue funding policy premiums, Mr. Braun initiated policy loans against two Northwestern Mutual whole life insurance policies starting in 2004. Upon attaining age 65, Mr. Braun contacted Northwestern Mutual to claim annuity distributions. The insurer informed him that the contracts contained no annuity provisions and that he had either misunderstood the terms or received inaccurate representations from the selling agent. During or prior to August 2018, Mr. Braun ceased paying premiums on both policies. Consequently, in August and December 2018, Northwestern Mutual issued written notifications informing him that, due to nonpayment, his whole life policies had been converted to term life insurance policies. The insurer’s correspondence explicitly noted that: Mr. Braun took no affirmative steps to pay the outstanding premiums, restore original coverage, or formally reject the conversion. Thereafter, Northwestern Mutual issued a Form 1099-R (Distributions From Pensions, Annuities, Retirement or Profit-Sharing Plans, IRAs, Insurance Contracts, etc.) for the 2018 tax year reporting a gross distribution of $214,291.52 and taxable income of $115,551.99. Mr. Braun timely filed his 2018 Form 1040 (U.S. Individual Income Tax Return) on April 15, 2019, reporting taxable income of $75,966 and tax liability of $18,313. Attached to the return was an explanatory statement indicating that he intentionally omitted the taxable amount reported on Form 1099-R because he received no physical cash distribution. Following an examination conducted through its Automatic Underreporter System, the IRS issued a Notice of Deficiency on April 12, 2021. The IRS determined an income tax deficiency of $29,202 resulting from unreported gross income of $115,551 (rounded down from $115,551.99) from Northwestern Mutual and $98 of unreported interest income ($80 from the IRS IMF and $18 from Wells Fargo Bank). Additionally, the IRS determined a $5,840 accuracy-related penalty under I.R.C. Section 6662(a). Mr. Braun timely filed a Petition with the U.S. Tax Court on July 16, 2021, seeking redetermination of the deficiency and accuracy-related penalty. In his petition and at trial, the taxpayer’s primary argument rested on cash-basis principles, asserting that he did not receive “even $1.00” from Northwestern Mutual in 2018. Because no funds were physically disbursed or deposited into his bank accounts, he contended that no taxable distribution occurred. Additionally, Mr. Braun testified that Northwestern Mutual committed “fraud” during the initial policy sales process and upon converting the policies to term life insurance. However, during cross-examination, Mr. Braun conceded that he had taken no legal or administrative actions against the insurer to assert fraud or rescind the contract conversion. Regarding the unreported interest income totaling $98, Mr. Braun failed to challenge the adjustment in his petition. Pursuant to Tax Court Rule 34(b)(1)(G), the Court deemed the interest income issue conceded by the taxpayer. The Court’s legal analysis commenced with I.R.C. Section 61(a), which establishes that gross income encompasses “all income from whatever source derived,” specifically including “income from life insurance and annuity contracts” under I.R.C. Section 61(a)(9). Treasury Regulation Section 1.61-1(a) reinforces that gross income includes income realized in any form unless specifically excluded by law. As reaffirmed in Commissioner v. Glenshaw Glass Co., 348 U.S. 426, 430 (1955), “The taxpayer has the burden of demonstrating that his accession to wealth is exempt from taxation.” While I.R.C. Section 101(a) excludes from gross income amounts received under a life insurance contract if paid by reason of the death of the insured, Judge Leyden observed that the proceeds in Braun were non-death benefits. Consequently, taxation is governed by I.R.C. Section 72(e). Under I.R.C. Section 72(e)(5)(A) and (C), non-death distributions received under a life insurance contract are included in gross income to the extent the amount received exceeds the taxpayer’s investment in the contract (basis). Basis generally equals aggregate premiums paid less prior non-taxable distributions. In evaluating policy loans, the Court highlighted established precedent establishing that policy loans secured by cash surrender value constitute valid indebtedness for tax purposes (Brown v. Commissioner, T.C. Memo. 2011-83, aff’d, 693 F.3d 765 (7th Cir. 2012); Minnis v. Commissioner, 71 T.C. 1049, 1054 (1979)). When a policy lapses or converts, and accumulated cash surrender value is applied to extinguish outstanding policy loans or acquire alternative coverage, the transaction is treated as a surrender. Where cash value exceeds net premium investment, the taxpayer constructively receives ordinary income taxable under I.R.C. Section 72(e) equal to cash surrender value minus aggregate premiums paid (Barr v. Commissioner, T.C. Memo. 2009-250). Applying these principles to Mr. Braun’s transaction, Judge Leyden emphasized that physical receipt of cash is not a prerequisite for gross income recognition under I.R.C. Section 61(a). The Court analyzed the Mechanics of the policy conversion: “The record in this case is clear that after petitioner stopped paying the premiums, Northwestern Mutual used to the cash value of the two original insurance policies to purchase term life insurance. Further, there was excess cash value (greater than the amount of the petitioner’s premium paid) when this occurred. The upshot of this was that petitioner was enriched because of the cash value of the original policies was greater than the amount of premiums he had paid.” Addressing the evidentiary burdens, the Court noted that under I.R.C. Section 7491(a), the burden of proof shifts to the Commissioner only if the taxpayer introduces credible evidence and satisfies statutory prerequisites. Because Mr. Braun presented no evidence or argument regarding I.R.C. Section 7491(a), the burden of proof regarding the deficiency remained entirely with him under Welch v. Helvering, 290 U.S. 111, 115 (1933) and Tax Court Rule 142(a). The Court further addressed information return matching under I.R.C. Section 6201(d). Under I.R.C. Section 6201(d), if a taxpayer raises a reasonable dispute regarding an item of income reported on a third-party Form 1099, the Commissioner bears the burden of producing reasonable and probative evidence beyond the information return. Judge Leyden concluded: “However, after trial and a review of the record in this case, petitioner has not provided any evidence to support a reasonable dispute with respect to the accuracy of the Form 1099-R. Consequently, the burden of production with respect to the income did not shift to respondent under section 6201(d).” Finally, Judge Leyden evaluated Mr. Braun’s claims of sales misrepresentations and contract fraud: “Petitioner asserted in his testimony that Northwestern committed ‘fraud’ when it sold him his policies and when it converted the policies into term life insurance, but petitioner acknowledged that he did not take any affirmative steps to reverse the conversion or to bring an administrative or legal action against Northwestern Mutual to assert fraud.” Because Mr. Braun failed to establish any applicable statutory exception or legal defense, the Tax Court sustained the Commissioner’s determination that Mr. Braun realized $115,551 of taxable ordinary income in 2018. Although the Commissioner prevailed on the deficiency issue, the Tax Court reached the opposite conclusion regarding the $5,840 accuracy-related penalty under I.R.C. Section 6662(a). Under I.R.C. Section 6662(a) and (b)(2), a 20% penalty applies to any portion of an underpayment attributable to a substantial understatement of income tax. Under I.R.C. Section 6662(d)(1)(A), an understatement is substantial if it exceeds the greater of 10% of the tax required to be shown on the return or $5,000. While Mr. Braun’s deficiency satisfied the threshold for substantial understatement, statutory burden-of-proof rules dictated the result. Under I.R.C. Section 7491(c), the Commissioner bears the burden of production in court proceedings regarding an individual’s liability for penalties or additions to tax. Furthermore, I.R.C. Section 6751(b)(1) mandates that no penalty shall be assessed unless the initial determination is approved in writing by the immediate supervisor of the individual making the determination, unless automatically calculated through electronic means. Judge Leyden emphasized that the Commissioner must affirmatively demonstrate compliance with I.R.C. Section 6751(b)(1). In striking down the penalty, Judge Leyden ruled: “However, under section 6751(b) respondent has the burden of providing evidence that the substantial understatement penalty in this case was either approved by the examiner’s supervisor or was automatically calculated by electronic means, and therefore exempt from the requirement of supervisory approval. While at trial respondent’s counsel asserted that she would provide evidence to meet this burden of proof, she did not. Therefore, the Court concludes that respondent has not met this burden of production and that petitioner is not liable for the section 6662(a) penalty.” The Tax Court concluded its bench opinion by entering a decision for the Commissioner regarding the $29,202 tax deficiency and entering a decision for the taxpayer regarding the $5,840 accuracy-related penalty: “To reflect the foregoing, a decision will be entered for respondent with respect to the deficiency and a decision will be entered for petitioner with respect to the accuracy-related penalty under section 6662(a).” For tax advisors, Braun v. title: Nearly Eight Years Later, the SoundExchange v. Music Choice Unpaid Royalties Battle Resumes - Digital Music News
content: SoundExchange fired off the original suit, centering on alleged underpayments between 2013’s start and 2016’s end, in April 2019. And as that filing date’s eight-year anniversary is only months away, a quick refresher is in order. The way the plaintiff tells the story, a Prager Metis audit, itself having spanned multiple years as Music Choice purportedly refused to provide “access to any information pertaining to its activities in 2013,” determined that the defendant had “systematically underpaid statutory royalties” on the above-noted business subscription. The short version is that a multifaceted disagreement erupted concerning the precise definition of “gross proceeds” in the relevant statutory text. Per SoundExchange, the DSP wrongfully omitted business-offering revenue (a percentage of which is owed for the license) tied to channels and recordings that were likewise provided under the non-business subscription. In brief, Music Choice allegedly “hid from SoundExchange the vast majority of the fees and payments it actually received from the provision of its” business tier. Fast forward to December 2021, when the presiding judge referred the case to the Copyright Royalty Board (CRB) for clarification, and then to December 2024, when the CRB largely agreed with SoundExchange in a voluminous ruling. (Among other things, SoundExchange had argued that Music Choice’s interpretation would allow for a large number of non-royalty-bearing usages when the recordings were added to the business and general subscriptions alike.) Music Choice quickly appealed, and the appropriate court this past August kicked the case back to the district court on jurisdictional grounds. “At this point, the Parties believe it would be beneficial to conduct discovery in phases to facilitate potential settlement discussions,” Music Choice and SoundExchange wrote, proceeding to propose “an approximately 75-day period of damages discovery culminating in settlement discussions or mediation.” Running with the corresponding suggested schedule, the litigants would have until early March to wrap the settlement talks or mediation. Time will tell whether the stretch delivers a resolution, though quite a lot has changed since the plodding dispute began. 15 months ago, in the SoundExchange v. SiriusXM royalties clash, a federal judge granted the satellite radio giant’s dismissal motion, concurring that the non-profit “has no private right of action under” the appropriate Copyright Act statute. Now, with other royalties actions on ice, an all-important appeal is underway, we broke down last month.

title: The People v. Gorilla Grodd Wraps; "More Intense" Jimmy Olsen: Gisondo - Bleeding Cool News
content: Posted in: HBO, Max, Movies, TV | Tagged: The People v. Gorilla Grodd Skyler Gisondo shared that filming on DC Studios' The People v. Gorilla Grodd has wrapped and discussed offering a "more intense" Jimmy Olsen. Set between Superman and Supergirl, and the upcoming Man of Tomorrow, Tony Yacenda and Dan Perrault's Skyler Gisondo (Superman)-starring The People v. Gorilla Grodd might just rank as one of DC Studios' more interesting efforts. Going the mockumentary route to introduce more of the DCU to viewers could be a lot of fun, especially with the creative team tapped for the project. Speaking with Deadline Hollywood about his current film, Primetime, Gisondo confirmed that "we just wrapped" filming, though he was cautious to offer more beyond that. "This is uncharted territory for me, and I don't know what I can say. I really don't want to get fired, and I really don't want to get in trouble [laughs]," he shared. "I can say American Vandal is one of my favorite shows of all time. Dan Perrault and Tony Yacenda, who were behind that show, are also behind this one. For what this show is, I don't think there was anybody else in the world who could have done it or who could have done what they would've done. I think it's an approach to this world that I've certainly never seen before. People can expect something different. In the movie, Jimmy, because you're getting a smaller dose of him, it's [not as big of a performance]. On the show, I can be a little more off-the-wall in some ways. I can take bigger swings," Gisondo continued. He added, "There's a difference between being a piece of the puzzle in a very big movie, where you can come in, take really big swings and try things, and being more at the center of a story. It's a different kind of thing. I think the stakes of the show are surprisingly big. It's deeply funny, and I think people are going to be surprised by the stakes, where it goes, and how big it gets. It's definitely a more intense version of Jimmy Olsen than we've seen before. I don't think I can get fired for anything I just said [laughs]." A superintelligent ape is convicted of murdering his father, the King of Gorilla City. In an eight-part "true" crime docuseries, the Daily Planet's Jimmy Olsen reopens the case, investigating whether Gorilla Grodd was wrongly convicted in one of Metropolis' most famous murder trials. The streaming series stars Skyler Gisondo as Jimmy Olsen, Jimmy Tatro as Gorilla Grodd, Beck Bennett as Steve Lombard, Mikaela Hoover as Cat Grant, and Wendell Pierce as Perry White. Additional cast includes Mary Holland, Eduardo Franco, Arian Moayed, Dan Perrault, Andrew Leeds, Tim Baltz, and (reportedly) Sara Gilbert. James Gunn and Peter Safran, executive producers and DC Studios' Co-Chairmen & Co-CEOs, shared, "Between Skyler's wonderful performance and the fantastic chemistry of the Daily Planet cast, we knew coming out of 'Superman' that this would be a fun world to explore. We're excited to work with the brilliant Dan Perrault and Tony Yacenda to take the audience down some of the darker and funnier streets and alleyways of the DCU as Jimmy spotlights the Metropolis criminal justice system for his docuseries." "We're excited by the challenge of creating a series that feels less like an entry into the DCU and more like an artifact from it. A Daily Planet original documentary made for the people of Metropolis. We hope it'll appeal to fans of the comics, comedy and true crime. And while we can't speak for audiences here yet, we already know it's a huge hit in Metropolis. They love this series," Tony Yacenda and Perrault added. Stemming from DC Studios in association with Warner Bros. Television, The People v. Gorilla Grodd is executive produced by James Gunn, Peter Safran, Tony Yacenda, and Dan Perrault. Yacenda and Perrault also serve as showrunners and writers, with all episodes directed by Yacenda.

title: Forget Firefly, Morena Baccarin's 2-Part Sci-Fi Remake Is an Undisputed Masterpiece - Comic Book Resources
content: Although Firefly was canceled after a single season, it has endured among fans, earning cult-classic status. The sci-fi space Western featured plenty of action, but it also had a slow-burn will-they-won't-they dynamic between Nathan Fillion’s Mal Reynolds and Morena Baccarin’s Inara Serra. Both went on to successful careers, and Baccarin even starred in another memorable sci-fi series, V, seven years later. V is a science fiction drama series that premiered on ABC and ran for two seasons. It is a remake of Kenneth Johnson's 1983 miniseries. At the time of the 2009 premiere, it received generally positive reviews from fans and critics. Sadly, though, V did not achieve the same legacy as Firefly, but it still deserves all the recognition. V stars Elizabeth Mitchell as Erica Evans, an FBI counterterrorism agent who becomes involved with the extraterrestrial "Visitors," and Morena Baccarin as Anna, the Visitors' queen and high commander. The sci-fi series centers on a massive alien invasion as spaceships enter Earth's atmosphere and hover above 29 major cities worldwide. Anna addresses the world, claiming they have come in peace. The Visitors need resources from Earth and, in exchange, offer medical and technological advancements. As far as alien invasion TV shows go, it's par for the course. Naturally, as humanity tends to do, many people doubt the extraterrestrials' generosity, leading to the involvement of FBI agent Erica Evans. As Agent Evans investigates the Visitors, she slowly uncovers a horrible truth about them. While they look completely human, they are actually terrifying reptilian humanoid creatures wearing false human disguises. They have been infiltrating Earth for years by posing as real human citizens, taking up important positions in government, law enforcement, big businesses, and even religious factions. Essentially, V takes the "lizard people" conspiracy theory and turns it into a real threat. Anna's invasion and occupation, on the surface, seems like Earth's first contact with the Visitors, but in reality, Anna has been formulating a hostile takeover for years. Sending the spaceships to occupy Earth's largest and most influential cities is the final step in her plan for complete global domination. This leads to the creation of the "Fifth Column," a resistance organization of humans and Visitors who sympathize with humanity enough to rebel against Anna. Erica learns the truth about the aliens and even meets Visitors who don't agree with Anna's plan, such as sleeper agent Ryan (Morris Chestnut), who has grown to love humanity after secretly living among them. Most of humanity welcomes the aliens. That's the most interesting part about V. As the Visitors offer cures for various deadly illnesses and sci-fi technology that humanity could only dream of, Anna succeeds in winning over the public's heart, making it even easier for her to execute her plan. Even Erica's own son ends up enamored by the Visitors' false kindness. Some critics and industry professionals interpreted V as an allegory for the campaign that President Barack Obama created before his election. This became a popular fan theory due to the way V aired on the anniversary of President Obama's inauguration, as well as common themes used by Anna and the Visitors that seemed reminiscent of Obama's platform. Ideas of hope and change for a better tomorrow, and even universal and accessible health care, were all promises made by Anna and the alien invaders. The cast and crew of V all denied these allegations, with many genuinely shocked that critics were interpreting V as a political allegory. Unfortunately, V seems to be a case of wrong place, wrong time, because this remake of a classic sci-fi miniseries, in retrospect, wasn't trying to send a negative message about the president currently holding office. Morena Baccarin herself said that she modeled Anna after politicians as a bracket term. Even on TV, politicians are often charismatic, make alluring promises to gain support, and have selfish, underlying motives. Since Anna is the queen of the Visitors and has been executing a years-long plot to infiltrate and take over the world, it makes sense that she would draw inspiration from politics. In a 2019 interview with AV Club, Baccarin addressed the motivation behind V. "I was excited about the possibility of the political statements that we could make with the show. Obviously, on a network show, we’re not going to get too much into politics, but I liked the idea," she said. Looking back on the series now, V reads as an allegory for the state of the world as it is, not a direct criticism of a specific person or administration. In V, the Visitors replace real-life humans who have been destroying the world and keeping humanity divided, one classic sci-fi war or radical political movement at a time. V criticizes modern politics and religion, and how easily the public is swayed by what they want to believe rather than by what is true. After two seasons, V faced cancellation on ABC. Enough fans rallied behind the old-school sci-fi series to attempt to get Season 3 picked up by another network, like TNT, but sadly, it never was. It's a shame, because V had such a strong premise. If it had been allowed to grow, it could have explored how deep the Visitors' influence ran throughout human history. The series might have made some powerful statements, but at the end of the day, it was an incredibly intriguing spaceship series that deserves more recognition. title: The Next Honda CR-V Hybrid Could Start Production in February 2027, and Its 10% Efficiency Gain Could Push AWD Models Past 40 MPG - Torque News
content: The next Honda CR-V Hybrid could start production in Canada in February 2027, earlier than planned, according to Nikkei Asia. Honda says its next-generation hybrid will be 10% more efficient, which could lift today's 37 mpg AWD CR-V Hybrid past 40 MPG. Honda has not confirmed the timing. Here is what the reports say, what a 10% gain means for your fuel bill, and whether it is worth waiting. We have covered the 2028 CR-V's timeline before, and the latest reporting adds more detail. The biggest new piece is how soon production could begin. What the Reports Say About the Next Honda CR-V Hybrid Motor1 reports that Honda's next-generation hybrid system and the next CR-V are both set to arrive in 2027. That means CR-Vs with the new hybrid powertrain could reach dealers sooner than expected. Nikkei Asia reports that production of the next CR-V in Canada will begin in February 2027, ahead of the original plan. Production at Honda's US plants would follow about a month later. Honda gave Motor1 a statement. "This was not announced by Honda." "While we cannot comment on specific future product plans, as outlined in our 2026 Business Update, Honda remains on track to introduce next-generation HEV models beginning in 2027, featuring an all-new hybrid system and platform," Honda said. Honda plans to bring the next-generation hybrid to 15 models between 2027 and 2030, either as the only powertrain or as an option. The Ridgeline is also a candidate, and the third-generation Ridgeline is expected in 2028, according to reports. The reports also suggest Acura will build a new small crossover based on the CR-V, likely the next RDX. Smaller models are expected to pair the hybrid system with a 1.5-liter or 2.0-liter four-cylinder, while larger models like the Pilot, Passport, and Ridgeline would use a V6. Honda scaled back its battery-electric plans earlier this year and is no longer aiming to go all electric by 2040. Hybrids are now at the center of its strategy. What a 10% Efficiency Gain Means for CR-V Hybrid MPG Today's CR-V Hybrid is rated at 37 mpg combined with AWD and 40 with front-wheel drive. A 10% gain would mean about 41 mpg with AWD and 44 with front-wheel drive, so AWD models would move past 40 MPG. Real-world results already vary with driving style, and owners say today's CR-V Hybrid can reach 43 mpg if you drive it gently. The new system should raise that ceiling further. In dollars, the gain is modest. At 12,000 miles a year and $3.50 a gallon, going from 37 to about 41 mpg saves roughly $100 a year. That would bring the CR-V Hybrid close to the 2026 Toyota RAV4 Hybrid, which is rated at 42 mpg combined with AWD. Honda also says the new hybrid will cost 30% less to build, which could help keep prices in check. High gas prices are pushing more shoppers toward hybrids, and the CR-V is Honda's best-selling model. That fits Honda's plan to make the CR-V Hybrid its most popular model. Toyota is adding pressure, too. The RAV4 and Camry are now hybrid only, including sportier versions like the RAV4 GR Sport. That is why many expect the next CR-V to go hybrid only. Honda has not confirmed whether a gas version will remain. Moving a production timeline forward carries risk. A new hybrid system and a new platform launching early leave less time to catch quality problems before buyers do. Should You Wait for the Next Honda CR-V or Buy Now? Buying now has real advantages. Current CR-V Hybrids carry Honda's 10-year, 150,000-mile head gasket coverage, and dealers may discount outgoing models as the new one nears. Waiting makes sense if you want the newest design and the efficiency gain. It may also bring fixes for owner complaints, like the wet arm washers that struggle to clear the windshield. For most shoppers, about $100 a year in fuel savings is not a reason to wait. Buy now if you need a vehicle, and wait if you want the new design and can hold out until spring 2027. If you are open to used, there are also the CR-V years owners say are the ones to own. Older models avoid the new technology entirely. Would a CR-V Hybrid that tops 40 MPG be worth waiting for, or would you buy the current model now? Tim Healey is an experienced automotive writer and editor from Chicago, IL. title: James V. Guell Obituary - Fond du Lac Reporter
content: James “Jimbo” Vincent Guell, age 61, of Fond du Lac, WI, passed away on November 5th, 2026, after a courageous battle with cancer, surrounded by his loving family. James was born on October 2nd, 1965, in Fond du Lac, WI to James and Peggy Guell. James was a proud graduate of St. Mary’s Springs in Fond du Lac. On February 14th, 1992, he married Paula Anderson, and together they shared 34 years of marriage. James dedicated many years working at Manowske Welding. As an avid outdoorsman, he found great joy in hunting and fishing. Above all, James cherished the time spent with his family and friends. Known for his outgoing nature, he was always ready to lend a hand to anyone in need, and his infectious laughter brought joy to everyone around him. James is survived by his beloved wife Paula, his children: Elizabeth (Mike) Nitz, Vincent (Dylan) Guell, Matthew Guell, and Steven (Emilee) Guell. His grandchildren: Taylor Giese, Maisie Guell, and Elsie Guell. His parents James and Peggy Guell. His siblings: Yvonne (Darin) Moon, Christine (Scott) Kratz, David (Bridget) Guell, and Blaise (Amanda) Guell, and other loved ones, including many nieces and nephews. James was preceded in death by his grandparents, Ralph and Margret Guell, and Charlie and Lucille Clark. VISITATION Friends and family may call from 2:00 – 4:00 PM on Saturday, November 14, 2026, at Kurki Funeral Chapel & Crematory, 31 East Division Street, Fond du Lac. A celebration of James’ life will follow at 4:00 PM, on Saturday, November 14, 2026, Kurki Funeral Chapel and Crematory. A private burial will be held at a later date for immediate family. James will be deeply missed and forever remembered by all who had the privilege of knowing and loving him. A special thank you to the SSM Health Cancer Care in Fond du Lac. title: 2024 Suzuki V-Strom 800 Buyer’s Guide [Specs, Price] - Ultimate Motorcycling
content: The 2024 Suzuki V-Strom 800 is the street-focused version of the off-road-ready V-Strom 800DE. It keeps the DE’s 776cc parallel twin and 5.3-gallon fuel tank, and the changes are aimed at pavement. The list price is $9899. A 19-inch cast aluminum front wheel replaces the DE’s 21-inch wire-spoke wheel. Pure-street Dunlop D614 tires are tubeless, unlike the DE’s tube-type tires. Braking is a big step up. Radially mounted 4-piston Nissin calipers work the 310mm front discs, replacing the DE’s conventionally mounted 2-piston calipers. The rear carries over with a 260mm disc and single-piston caliper. The Showa suspension is simplified. The V-Strom 800 has a hair under six inches of wheel travel at both ends, compared to 8.7 inches on the DE, and the fork and shock have fixed damping and adjustable spring preload. The geometry is more aggressive to match. Rake is 26 degrees, two degrees steeper than the DE, and the wheelbase is 2.2 inches shorter at 59.6 inches. Ergonomics follow the same mission. The seat height drops 1.2 inches to 32.5 inches, and the narrower handlebar puts the grips farther forward for a more aggressive street stance. Rubber-covered aluminum footpegs replace the DE’s steel pegs. The liquid-cooled DOHC twin has 270-degree crankshaft timing and a broad powerband, pulling linearly from just above idle to its 9500-rpm redline. The 6-speed transmission has a quickshifter, and the clutch has assist-and-slipper functions. Dirt roads call for care, given 7.3 inches of ground clearance and no protective cowling. The V-Strom 800 is for riders who want adventure-bike versatility on paved roads. Suzuki keeps the color choice simple with Metallic Matte Steel Green. © tagDiv. All Rights Reserved. Fox News correspondent David Spunt has the latest on the DOJ launching a federal investigation into the 2022 leak of the Supreme Court's draft opinion overturning Roe v. Wade on 'America Reports.' The leak that exposed the U.S. Supreme Court’s (SCOTUS) draft opinion overturning Roe v. Wade is under criminal investigation by the Department of Justice (DOJ), years after the court’s own hunt for the culprit came up empty. U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro’s Washington, D.C., office is leading the probe, multiple sources briefed on the matter told Fox News on Wednesday. The investigation has been underway for at least a year, sources said, and comes three years after an investigation by SCOTUS failed to identify the culprit who leaked a draft of the 2022 decision. Grand jury subpoenas have been issued during the probe, though it is unclear who received them. SUPREME COURT LITIGATION FAILS TO IDENTIFY LEAKER OF DOBBS DRAFT DECISION An investigation by the Supreme Court three years ago was unable to determine who leaked a draft opinion overturning the federal constitutional right to abortion. (Kevin Carter/Getty Images, File) The New York Times first reported the investigation. Politico published the draft before the June 2022 ruling, prompting Chief Justice John Roberts to order an internal investigation that failed to identify the leaker. The DOJ and the U.S. Attorney’s Office declined to comment on the investigation. Fox News also reached out to the Supreme Court, asking whether the court or any justices have worked with outside investigators, including DOJ, or plan to do so. The criminal probe comes as Justice Samuel Alito says he has an idea who was responsible but lacks sufficient evidence to publicly identify that person. SUPREME COURT OVERTURNS ROE V. WADE IN LANDMARK ABORTION DECISION Chief Justice John Roberts had called upon the marshal of the court to investigate the leak. (Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images, File) "I do have an opinion. But the evidence available at this time is not strong enough for the court or for me to say this is the person who was responsible," Alito told Fox News chief legal correspondent and "Fox News Sunday" anchor Shannon Bream in an exclusive interview last month. "It was a grave breach of the trust that everybody who worked in this building had before that point. "And it very predictably made the five of us in the majority targets for assassination and nearly resulted in the assassination of my colleague Brett Kavanaugh." Politico published the draft on May 2, 2022, revealing that at least five conservative justices were prepared to overturn Roe. The final decision in Dobbs v. Jackson Women’s Health Organization followed on June 24, 2022, ending the nationwide constitutional right to abortion. Roberts tasked Court Marshal Gail Curley with investigating the leak. After months of forensic analysis and interviews with nearly 100 employees, the court announced in January 2023 that investigators were "unable to identify a person responsible by a preponderance of the evidence." LATEST SCOTUS LEAK A GIFT TO LIBERALS ‘SALIVATING’ OVER CONTROL OF HIGH COURT NARRATIVE: EXPERTS The probe comes as Justice Samuel Alito says he has an idea who was responsible.  (J. Scott Applewhite/AP Photo, File) "No one confessed to publicly disclosing the document and none of the available forensic and other evidence provided a basis for identifying any individual as the source of the document," the marshal’s report concluded. Multiple sources previously told Fox News that investigators had narrowed their inquiry into approximately 70 people who may have had access to the draft. Much of the initial focus was on roughly three dozen law clerks who worked directly with the justices. Fox News was also told at the time that Curley asked several permanent court employees who may have had access to the draft to turn over their cellphones and electronic devices. Supreme Court law clerks typically serve one-year terms for individual justices, meaning those who worked for the court when the draft leaked have since completed their clerkships. SUPREME COURT CHIEF JUSTICE PINPOINTS WHAT AMERICANS MISUNDERSTAND ABOUT HIM AND HIS COLLEAGUES The Supreme Court Jan. 13, 2026, in Washington.  (AP Photo/Julia Demaree Nikhinson, File) Roberts brought in former Homeland Security Secretary Michael Chertoff, a former federal appeals judge, to assess the court’s investigative methods. Chertoff concluded the investigation was thorough. "At this time, I cannot identify any additional useful investigative measures," Chertoff said. The marshal’s report also found it unlikely that someone outside the court had improperly accessed its computer systems. Investigators examined court devices, networks, printers and available call and text logs without finding forensic evidence identifying the source. The report found that expanded work-from-home arrangements during the coronavirus pandemic and gaps in security policies made it easier to remove sensitive information from the building and the court’s networks. Pro-abortion activists participate in the "Rally for Our Freedom" in Orlando, Fla. (Chandan Khanna/AFP via Getty Images, File) Some employees also admitted telling a spouse or partner about the draft, violating the court’s confidentiality rules, according to the report. The leak prompted protests outside justices’ homes and deepened distrust inside the court. A California man was arrested near Kavanaugh’s Maryland home in 2022 and charged with attempting to assassinate him. "When you lose that trust, especially in the institution that I’m in, it changes the institution fundamentally," Justice Clarence Thomas said shortly after the leak. "You begin to look over your shoulder." Fox News Digital's Bradford Betz contributed to this report. title: Film Quote of the Day: The ‘V for Vendetta’ Line That Made November 5th Unforgettable - No Film School
content: "Remember, remember the fifth of November, the gunpowder, treason, and plot." I vividly remember going to Regal Downingtown on opening night to see the new movie written by the Wahchoski siblings and directed by James McTeigue, based on one of my favorite Alan Moore graphic novels. It was an insane mix of anarchy and entertainment, steeped in Guy Fawkes lore and specific dates I recall every year, thanks to some catchy quotes. So, how did this movie use seventeenth-century British history to bridge cinematic pop culture and become a brain worm we repeat this time of year? This is one of those movies that grips you right from the get-go. We're in darkness, and then Evey Hammond (Natalie Portman) begins a quiet narration as we get the real Guy Fawkes's historical backstory. On November 5th, 1605, Guy Fawkes and his fellow conspirators attempted to blow up the House of Lords in the famous Gunpowder Plot, but the plan went awry when someone sent an anonymous letter to the authorities, and they found Guy with all the incriminating evidence. Whoops. This history gets juxtaposed against the authoritarian state Evey deals with right now. She invites the audience to consider why we remember the man behind the plot rather than the political machinery that condemned him to death for trying to fix a broken system. And then we get our famous line, the Guy Fawkes line that has been uttered for many years since his demise. The line that kicks off the story. This is one of those fun times when the quote has real historical context. I'd encourage you to spend some time reading about Guy Fawkes and get sme historical context, which will only make you appreciate the movie more. Anyway, all this is to say that when screenwriters Lilly and Lana Wachowski used the Fawkes saying, they bridged historical reality with a dystopian future. They delivered the thematic spine of what matters. Now, obviously, Alan Moore laid the tracks in the graphic novel, but this adaptation works because it identified that core and brought it to the screen. The opening scene directly tells us what the movie is about and infuses it with energy by reviving an old quote through the circumstances of fiction. We want to know how this plays into Evey's story moving forward. This explores people who have had enough and are willing to fight back. They are an enduring power that lives on, even in death, because they offer a vision for change. We open on November 5th because it symbolically continues an unfinished historical impulse that will carry the movie and its characters. I really like how we dive in and hear it echo in our minds as the story soldiers onward. Now, I don't know that I think about V for Vendetta every November 5th, but when that quote comes up, I do. We get this sort of dramatic recall that takes us back to this movie and the imagery of the Guy Fawkes mask.

title: Michael Wolff v. the First Lady - The East Hampton Star
content: One year ago, The Star reported on Melania Trump’s threat to sue the author and journalist Michael Wolff for $1 billion if he did not retract and apologize for statements linking her to the late financier and pedophile Jeffrey Epstein. Mr. Wolff, who with his family moved from Manhattan to Amagansett during the Covid-19 pandemic, countered that threat by bringing a lawsuit in State Supreme Court accusing the first lady of trying to stifle his inquiry into Epstein, suppressing his reporting on a matter of public concern. Mrs. Trump had referred to an article based on “Trump’s Epstein Scandal Can’t Stop Won’t Stop,” an episode of The Daily Beast’s “Inside Trump’s Head” podcast, which Mr. Wolff co-hosts. The Daily Beast retracted the article following a complaint from Mrs. Trump, writing that it “did not meet our standards and has therefore been removed from our platforms.” In his lawsuit, Mr. Wolff relied on New York State’s anti-SLAPP law (Strategic Lawsuits Against Public Participation). SLAPP lawsuits —  litigation tactics intended to silence critics and force time-consuming and expensive legal procedures — have long been employed by President Trump. New York’s anti-SLAPP legislation protects against meritless lawsuits aimed at suppressing free speech on matters of public interest. Mr. Wolff is the author of books including “Fire and Fury: Inside the Trump White House,” published in 2018, and “Too Famous: The Rich, the Powerful, the Wishful, the Notorious, the Damned” from 2022, which includes a long essay titled “The Last Days of Jeffrey Epstein.” In the 1990s, he was a media columnist for New York magazine and more recently wrote for The Hollywood Reporter. He has long known the president, and previously told The Star that he had met Epstein a few times while working for New York magazine. His own name appears repeatedly in the so-called Epstein files. Mr. Wolff sued Mrs. Trump in New York State Supreme Court after receiving a Florida pre-suit libel notice demanding a retraction and apology. Mrs. Trump successfully moved the case to a federal court, asserting “diversity jurisdiction,” which allows that court to hear a civil lawsuit when the dispute is between parties from different states. The move was necessary, she maintained, because she is a resident of Florida and not New York. Mr. Wolff argued that Mrs. Trump was indeed a New York resident, citing her residence at Trump Tower in Manhattan, ongoing ties via property ownership, and continuous time spent in the state. In May, rather than decide the case, the federal district court dismissed it, reasoning that Mr. Wolff should wait to see “if and when” Mrs. Trump actually sued him for defamation. Mr. Wolff filed a notice of appeal in June. On Friday, his lawyers asked the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit to reverse the federal court and send the case back to New York. “This action arises from an effort to silence” Mr. Wolff’s reporting, the legal brief states. “The gravamen of the Complaint is to protect Mr. Wolff’s free-speech rights under the New York Constitution, the First Amendment, and New York anti-SLAPP law to preserve his ability to continue reporting on the Trumps and the Epstein matter without the chilling effect of Mrs. Trump’s threats.” The federal court’s determination “in effect, gags the speech of a journalist on matters of utmost public concern,” the brief argues. Mrs. Trump is not a public official, it continues, “yet this action unavoidably implicates the public’s entitlement to information about its government. The speech being suppressed concerns the extent of the sitting President and First Lady’s relationship with child sex offender and human trafficker Jeffrey Epstein.” Along with the assertion that Mrs. Trump has yet to provide clear and convincing evidence that she has changed her residency to Florida, the brief charges that “the district court abused its discretion by assuming supplemental jurisdiction over Mr. Wolff’s affirmative anti-SLAPP claim — only to dismiss this action.” The dismissal leaves him facing the “chilling effect” of the threatened defamation suit without an adjudication of his rights, it concludes. Should the Court of Appeals side with Mr. Wolff, who seeks costs, attorney’s fees, and damages under New York Civil Rights Law, it could order the case returned to State Supreme Court, which would allow his anti-SLAPP claim to be heard without having to wait for a defamation lawsuit from Mrs. Trump, or at minimum require further fact-finding about her legal residency. title: Brighton and Hove Albion v Brentford: Match preview, kick-off time and more - Brentford FC
content:
Analysis, team news, match officials and more. Here's everything you need to know ahead of Brentford's Premier League game against Brighton and Hove Albion at American Express Stadium on Sunday (2pm kick-off GMT) Analysis, team news, match officials and more – here’s everything you need to know ahead of the game. Brentford make the short trip south to the Amex on Sunday for a fascinating clash against third-placed Brighton. The Seagulls have started the season in free-scoring fashion, netting 24 Premier League goals across the opening nine matchweeks – more than any other team in the division. Renowned for their astute recruitment and tactical adaptability, the south coast club have continued to flourish this term despite a couple of high-profile departures. The decision to re-sign Pascal Groß for just over £1 million at the start of the year has proved particularly inspired, with the 35-year-old's incisive passing and game intelligence central to much of Brighton's best attacking work. The German playmaker has already registered four assists this season, moving into the Premier League's all-time top 50 for assists, and also leads the division with 24 key passes. Between them, Brighton (11) and Brentford (10) have had 21 different Premier League goalscorers this season, underlining the variety of attacking options that will be on show at the Amex. One area in which the Seagulls have been particularly effective is set-pieces. Brighton have already scored seven times from corners, free-kicks and throw-ins in 2026/27 – more than any other Premier League side and just four fewer than they managed throughout last season. While Brighton's set-piece prowess represents a significant improvement on last season, their ability to regain possession high up the pitch remains one of their defining features. Long known for their aggressive, high-intensity pressing, Brighton once again rank among the Premier League's most effective sides out of possession. Fabian Hürzeler's side start their passing sequences higher up the pitch than any other team in the division and rank second for pressing sequences (123), while their 8.8 passes allowed per defensive action is also the second-lowest figure in the top flight. Interestingly, the only side ahead of Brighton in both categories is Tottenham, now managed by former Seagulls boss Roberto De Zerbi. That relentless pressure has helped Brighton force a league-leading 97 high turnovers this season, underlining their ability to disrupt opponents attempting to play out from the back. Brentford will therefore need to be alert defensively, but Brighton's underlying numbers offer Keith Andrews and his side some encouragement at the other end of the pitch. Only Arsenal (five) have conceded fewer Premier League goals than Brighton (seven) this season, but the Seagulls' expected goals against figure of 13.34 suggests opponents have created considerably more than their impressive defensive record might indicate. Brighton’s European push only started to gain real momentum in February, when they beat Brentford 2-0 in west London. The Seagulls had only won one of the 13 Premier League matches leading up to that - but it was the first in a run of six wins in eight games that lifted them right back into the mix. A second successive eighth-place finish - and qualification for the Conference League - was the eventual reward, but with just one more point, they would have returned to the Europa League. Still, Brighton know European football of any kind is precious. They reached the Europa League last 16 in 2023/24 under Roberto De Zerbi, but found competing on multiple fronts a challenge. This time, they have a stronger squad and experience under their belts. They are outright favourites to win the Conference League for a reason. In September, owner Tony Bloom said: “We’re after a major trophy”. Even so, they might well have bigger fish to fry. Nine games into the 2026/27 Premier League season, Fabian Hürzeler's side are third in the table. They are two points behind Man City and five behind Arsenal – having already beaten both. They have scored 24 goals, which is the most in the division, and conceded seven, which is the second fewest in the division. And they are averaging 2.11 points per game. Based on that average, they would pick up another 61 points this season, which would take them to 80. For context, their record points tally in the Premier League is 62 (2022/23) and 80 has been enough for a top-three finish in five of the last six seasons. Of course, nine games is a small sample size in the grand scheme of things and Brighton will, by no means, be getting carried away. After the November international break, they have 11 games before the turn of the year. That equates to one game every 3.7 days. This is where the depth of their squad will be truly put to the test. For now, it’s about enjoying this incredible start and building solid foundations for later down the line. If Brighton do end up being in the title race, it would be an incredible achievement and one unthinkable for many until relatively recently. Yet even if that becomes unmanageable in the long run, the potential to qualify for the Champions League and/or win a European trophy would still represent another remarkable step forward for a club that continues to raise its own ceiling. Born in February 1993, during the time his Swiss father and German mother were working in the USA, Fabian Hürzeler started out as part of Bayern Munich's youth system after returning to Europe aged 2. He spent the best part of a decade with Die Roten, working his way up to play for Bayern Munich II, while also playing for the German national team from U15 to U19 level. Hürzeler moved on in 2013, first to 1899 TSG Hoffenheim II, then to 1860 Munich II a year later, before dropping to the fifth tier of German football with Pipinsried, where he combined playing with the role of head coach, while also working as assistant manager of Germany U18s and U20s. His coaching credentials were clear from the start, as Pipinsreid won promotion from the Bayernliga Sud in his first season. After four years, he left the club in the summer of 2020 and was appointed assistant at St Pauli. Two-and-a-half years later - aged just 29 - he became head coach after the departure of Timo Schulz, four months before he was granted his UEFA Pro Licence, and led the club to a fifth-place finish in the 2. Bundesliga in 2022/23. Hürzeler's side flourished in 2023/24 and went unbeaten in their first 20 games of the season, on the way to pipping Holstein Kiel to the title by a single point to secure a return to the Bundesliga after 13 years away. Just three months after signing a new contract at St Pauli in March 2024, Hürzeler took over from Roberto De Zerbi at Brighton, becoming the Premier League's youngest permanent manager in history at the age of 31. At 33, Hürzeler remains the youngest manager in the top four divisions of English football. Brian Owen, Brighton and Hove Albion reporter at The Argus, explains how Fabian Hürzeler is likely to set his side up for Sunday’s game against Brentford. “Officially, you would probably say 4-2-3-1, but Enzo Maresca made the point ahead of the game against Man City last week, and he is right, that they do go direct more often. “They are very intense, relentless, and they have made a point of being physically stronger this season as well. “Players crop up in all sorts of positions, especially the full-backs.” Last Premier League starting XI v Manchester City (4-2-3-1): Verbruggen; Costinha, Vušković, Dunk, Boscagli; Groß, Andrés; Gómez, Ayari, De Cuyper; Kostoulas Yehor Yarmoliuk is available for Sunday’s game at Brighton after completing his three-match suspension. Head coach Keith Andrews reported no fresh injury concerns following the win over Nottingham Forest. Josh Dasilva is edging closer to a first-team return after featuring alongside Yarmoliuk for Brentford B on Monday. Antoni Milambo has trained consistently but is not yet ready for selection. Fábio Carvalho (knock) and Rico Henry (hip and quad) remain sidelined. Michael Oliver will referee Sunday’s game at the Amex. Oliver was the man in the middle for Brentford’s 3-0 victory over Tottenham Hotspur on the opening day of the Premier League season. Oliver has officiated 13 games this season, showing 39 yellow cards and four reds. Brentford were denied all three points against Brighton and Hove Albion by Alexis Mac Allister’s last-minute penalty. The Bees took the lead three times only to be pegged back on each occasion in a thrilling encounter on the south coast. Pontus Jansson nodded home after 10 minutes; a goal which was cancelled out 11 minutes later by Kaoru Mitoma’s neat lob. That kicked off a spell of three goals in seven minutes which saw Ivan Toney restore the Bees’ advantage before Danny Welbeck’s close-range leveller. Ethan Pinnock put Brentford back ahead at the start of the second half; a lead which lasted until Mac Allister’s spot-kick in the final minute of normal time. Vantage London

title: U.S. v. Parasmo Brief: A Wrong Jury Instruction Is Not Harmless Where the Defendant Presented Believable Evidence of Innocence - Cato Institute
content: Sign up to have blog posts delivered straight to your inbox! Dr. Frank Parasmo is an 80-year-old physician who practiced in New York for decades. A federal jury convicted him of unlawfully distributing controlled substances based on his prescription of opioids to patients experiencing chronic pain. The case was close. Unlike in many other cases, Dr. Parasmo was able to put forward extensive evidence that his practice was not a so-called “pill mill.” As a dissenting judge later noted, Dr. Parasmo “ordered numerous tests, referred his patients to a wide variety of specialists to treat their pain inducing conditions, tried to wean them off the controlled substances, and looked for alternative treatments to control his patients’ pain, including prescribing medications other than a controlled substance—all behaviors suggestive of a good faith effort to help his patients.” But over Dr. Parasmo’s objection, the jury was instructed that his intent turned on whether he “was (objectively) ‘acting reasonably’” rather than whether he subjectively intended to overprescribe. Applying that objective standard, the jury issued a split verdict, convicting him on some counts while acquitting him on others. Following the trial, the Supreme Court held in another case that a conviction requires proof that the defendant subjectively knew he was acting in an unauthorized manner. On appeal, the Second Circuit acknowledged that the district court’s intent instruction was wrong but, in a divided decision, deemed the error harmless. It reached that conclusion by reviewing the government’s evidence presented at trial and determining that it “overwhelmingly” supported a finding of subjective intent. But as Judge Robinson explained in her dissent, that was not the appropriate inquiry. The panel should have instead looked to the “ample evidence” the defense put forward and asked whether a “jury could have concluded” that Dr. Parasmo lacked the requisite intent. Cato joined an amicus brief filed by the National Legal Aid & Defender Association, Due Process Institute, and National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers asking the Supreme Court to take Dr. Parasmo’s case and reverse the Second Circuit’s decision. In the words of Judge Robinson, the erroneous jury instruction—and the Second Circuit’s finding of harmless error—“took the central contested factual issue … away from the jury.” This is exactly what the Constitution prohibits in guaranteeing those accused of a crime a trial by jury. Where the defendant contested an element of the accusation against him and a juror could rationally conclude that the prosecution had failed to meet its burden on that element, incorrect jury instruction is not harmless error that can be excused by judges. Every weekday morning: independent analysis grounded in individual liberty, limited government, free markets, and peace.
